probes.support_reason: Deterministic tie-break, all-yes. (1) `open("data.txt")` opens the named file for reading using only a built-in, and the operation can fail - the contract states 'If the file cannot be opened, an OSError is raised', verified on the host by removing data.txt, which produced FileNotFoundError. (2) `text = f.read()` reads the entire contents into a TEXT-STRING local; the default mode 'r' is text mode, so `text` is a `str`. (3) The `with` statement guarantees release when the enclosing scope ends INCLUDING when step (2) fails: Language Reference 8.5 calls `__exit__` on every exit path, and the io documentation states 'file is closed after the with statement's suite is finished - even if an exception occurs'. Witness stored at semantic-compression/probes/witnesses/F17.P1/python/release_on_failure_path.py: with a reader whose `read` raises, the handle was closed exactly once and the exception propagated. (4) `return len(text.encode())` returns the length in BYTES - `str.encode` is written explicitly because Python's `len` on a `str` counts CHARACTERS, not bytes, so `len(text)` would have silently delivered a different quantity; and the open/read failure is propagated 'in whatever way that language's mechanism requires', which for Python is implicitly, since exceptions propagate with no declaration and the fragment installs no handler. F-2/F-4: built-ins and the standard io module only, no package, no flag beyond `python3 FILE.py`. F-3: runs and prints 6 for the 6-byte data.txt ('hello\n'). F-6: no sentence of the Library Reference places `open`, the `with` statement, `read`, `encode` or `len` under a normative prohibition or deprecation. R10 evidence: (a) THE MEASURED FORM = 29 tokens; (b) the `try: f = open(...) ... finally: f.close()` spelling = 36 tokens, and it is the form the io documentation itself advises against ('It is good practice to use the with keyword when dealing with file objects'), so R10 and the documentation order both select (a); (c) the same form with the `return` INSIDE the with suite = 29 tokens, an exact tie, broken toward the measured form because closing the handle BEFORE computing and returning the result is the ordering the with-statement documentation presents; (d) `with open("data.txt") as f: return len(f.read().encode())` = 26 tokens, the fewest of any spelling, but rejected under R1 rather than R10, because it binds NO local named `text` and sub-requirement (2) names that local explicitly. OBSERVATION TARGET (non-normative): a reader CAN determine WHERE the release happens - the `with` token names it at the acquisition site - and that it happens exactly once on every exit path, because 8.5 states it; what the reader CANNOT see locally is that the object `open` returns is a context manager at all, which is why a hop to the io contract is charged below. Witness: the frozen file runs under `python3 FILE.py` and prints 1.

Cached-object reading: Language Reference 3.1 lets an implementation return an existing object of the same type and value for an immutable type, so `released + 1` may bind a pre-existing int and allocate nothing at that site (A8 = no observable resource event there). Distinguishable with `is`. Witness: with `released = 0` the result `1 is 1` holds on CPython 3.14.5, while starting the counter above 256 produces a fresh object.

determinacy_enumeration: First-import, fresh-object reading: `import util` finds and EXECUTES the unit's top-level code, binds the module object, and the qualified call runs the `pub_add` defined in it, producing a newly created int 6. A1 = the module and the arguments are denoted by references, never copied, A2 = the import writes `sys.modules`, A4 = arbitrary-precision integer, A7 = the target is the `def` in the second unit, A8 = allocation at the import and at each addition, A9 = falls through. Witness: the frozen pair runs and prints 6.

Cached-module reading: Language Reference 5.3 checks `sys.modules` first and executes a module's code only on the first import, so the same fragment is equally compatible with an execution in which the import statement runs NO module code at all and merely binds a module object that already exists (A2 = `sys.modules` unchanged, A8 = no resource event at the import). Materially different under Rule 1.2.1 - whether the unit's top-level code executes at this span differs - and observable. Witness: importing `util` from the wrapper BEFORE the fragment (outside the measured region) makes the fragment's own `import util` execute nothing, which a print placed in util.py outside its markers detects.

Cached-int reading: Reference 3.1 lets an implementation return an existing object of the same type and value for an immutable type, so the additions may bind pre-existing ints and allocate nothing (A8 = no observable resource event at those sites). Distinguishable with `is`. Witness: `util.pub_add(2, 3) is 6` evaluates True on CPython 3.14.5 (small-int cache) while the same call with operands above 256 evaluates False.

Different-unit reading: WHICH module the name `util` binds is decided by `sys.path` and `sys.modules`, both of which are whole-program state outside the measured fragment, so under Rule 1.1.2 they are external. A different `util` earlier on the path supplies a different `pub_add` - A2 = arbitrary state written, A4 = any type, A8 = arbitrary resource events, A9 = may not return - none of which the in-region definition can reach. Rule 1.4.7 counts this because it enables otherwise unreachable classes. Witness: placing a different util.py earlier on sys.path makes the same fragment print a different value, with both marked regions unchanged.
